canonical_topic: Compressed-Air Thermal Storage as a Peak/Off-Peak Spread Position
definition: Using a compressed-air-based HVAC system that compresses air overnight (off-peak) so daytime (peak) cooling load is met without buying peak power, which turns an operating decision into a financial spread position between peak and off-peak electricity prices.
core_idea: Installing an HVAC system that shifts electricity consumption from peak to off-peak hours is financially equivalent to being long peak power and short off-peak power; separately arranging a supply contract for the off-peak leg cancels that exposure, leaving a pure long position in peak prices.
key_points: The compressor does not need to run in real time — air can be compressed overnight and used during the day.
Because the buyer purchases power wholesale, it can arrange a contract to buy specifically off-peak.
The investment becomes more valuable if peak prices rise after installation, and also benefits if the contracted off-peak price falls.
Locking in the off-peak purchase price removes that leg's price risk, isolating the position to peak-price exposure.
The author notes this is a piece of physical hardware, not purely a financial instrument, even though it can be analyzed as one.
trading_implications: Once the off-peak leg is contracted away, the investment's value tracks the peak power price level.
A physical efficiency/hardware investment can be analyzed and hedged like a financial spread trade.
caveats: Viewing this purely as an operating-cost saving rather than as a market-price-exposed peak/off-peak spread position.
